info.title: PlaneMem saved ContextPack metadata directory
info.description: Source-only description of the existing GET /v1/context-packs operation. This document covers only saved-pack metadata listing, not the complete WCP API. No validator, generator or runtime verification was executed. Load this document and the adjacent ../schemas/context-pack-directory.json resource locally, preserving relative paths and registering the schema's full $id; do not fetch planemem.local.

servers.description: Use the intended Gateway origin; no deployed host is implied.

tags.name: Saved ContextPack directory
tags.description: Current permission-filtered saved metadata; content and sources are not read.

get.summary: List one page of saved ContextPack metadata
get.description: Require a verified unexpired Bearer session, complete scope/actor/client and normalized context.read capability. Existing workbench authentication may map workbench.read or its designated client's Base capability to context.read; admin alone is insufficient. The Gateway checks the parent project and filters saved read_restricted buckets using data.restricted.read before paging. Records contain only version, pack_id, created_at, expires_at, budget_tokens and used_tokens; expired/stale packs may appear and an exact absent or invisible pack returns an empty page. An unavailable parent project returns 404. Sort by version descending then pack_id ASCII/C descending; the cursor binds identity, scope, roles/capabilities, page size and exact filter. Preserve those conditions for continuation; it is not a credential or a cross-page snapshot. Query fields must occur at most once; unknown/empty/null fields are rejected. Do not send a body, transfer-encoding, write conditions, conditional-cache headers or Range. Content-length must be absent or the literal 0. The response never includes ETag, revision or content/hash/source manifests. Inspect a full pack through its separate read operation when needed. HTTP expected identity headers are independently optional; CLI's paired JSON constraints are a different input contract.

x-runtime-limits.description: Annotations only, enforced by existing code. Parsed query budget is not a raw URL byte limit. Handler deadline excludes outer authentication, authorization/audit and response sending. Timed-out database work retains its slot until it settles. Client error readers impose their own 16 KiB limits; no global server error-size guarantee is asserted.

parameters.name: pack_id
parameters.description: Optional exact saved pack ID. Empty is invalid; omit to list all visible metadata. At most one result, with no next_cursor, when provided.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, default 25. On the wire use one canonical positive decimal integer 1..100: no sign, leading zero, fraction, exponent or whitespace. Response query always echoes the normalized integer. Changing the limit invalidates an existing cursor binding.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque original next_cursor for explicit continuation with unchanged conditions. Omit on the first page; empty is invalid. Runtime decodes and re-encodes the canonical base64url position and verifies its binding; lexical validity alone is insufficient. Restart without cursor when original conditions change.

200.description: Complete metadata page, including a valid empty page. The complete JSON envelope is at most 256 KiB. Every original scope/query/trace/source binding, record and page position is checked by the shared parser. No ETag is sent and conditional requests are rejected rather than producing 304.

x-trace-id.description: Required on successful directory reads; equals body.trace_id and the selected inbound trace.

400.description: INVALID_INPUT for unknown/repeated/invalid query, forbidden body or condition headers, or invalid/changed cursor binding; retryable=false. Early input rejection may omit x-trace-id; use body.trace_id. Unexpected boundary errors retain the shared error envelope.

401.description: UNAUTHENTICATED for missing or rejected Bearer credentials; retryable=false. This early authentication response does not guarantee x-trace-id or WWW-Authenticate headers. Renew the intended session explicitly.

403.description: DENIED for scope or expected-identity mismatch, policy/capability denial, missing valid actor/client or a session that expires before completion; retryable=false. Early authentication/identity denial may omit x-trace-id.

404.description: CONTEXT_PACK_NOT_FOUND when the parent project is unavailable or not visible; retryable=false. A missing/invisible exact pack within a visible project instead yields 200 with an empty data array.

429.description: RATE_LIMITED: shared actor/path request-rate limiter sets retryable=true; occupied two-slot directory handler capacity sets retryable=false. No Retry-After header or automatic retry is promised.

500.description: CONTEXT_PACK_INVALID for invalid or incomplete stored metadata/page (retryable=false), or INTERNAL_ERROR for an unexpected command failure (generic serializer uses retryable=true). No partial page is returned.

503.description: CONTEXT_PACK_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE or CONTEXT_PACK_DIRECTORY_TIMEOUT set retryable=false; WORKBENCH_AUTH_UNAVAILABLE and AUDIT_PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE set retryable=true. The authentication path may omit x-trace-id. Timeout stops waiting but does not cancel SQL or release occupied capacity before underlying work ends.

default.description: Other application boundary errors retain the shared error shape. This does not guarantee the format of errors produced by proxies or HTTP parsing before the application.

GatewayBearer.description: Send Authorization: Bearer <token>. The Gateway verifies issuer/session claims and expiration. Scope headers select and constrain an authorized project; actor/client/roles/capabilities come from verified claims. This scheme declares transport syntax, not authorization or an OAuth acquisition flow.

TenantId.name: x-tenant-id
TenantId.description: Requested tenant; must match the verified authorized scope.

WorkspaceId.name: x-workspace-id
WorkspaceId.description: Requested workspace; must match the verified authorized scope.

ProjectId.name: x-project-id
ProjectId.description: Requested project; must match the verified authorized scope. The visible parent project is checked on every page.

TraceParent.name: traceparent
TraceParent.description: The current runtime treats this as an opaque trace identifier and prefers a nonempty value over x-trace-id. It does not perform W3C Trace Context parsing here. Must satisfy the shared trace rule for a successful read.

TraceId.name: x-trace-id
TraceId.description: Used when traceparent is absent/empty. If neither has a nonempty value, the server generates trace_http_<ULID>. Prefer supplying one trace header; success echoes the selected value in the response body and x-trace-id.

ExpectedActorId.name: x-expected-actor-id
ExpectedActorId.description: Optional equality constraint on the verified actor, never an identity input. HTTP permits this independently of the client constraint. A mismatch yields DENIED.

ExpectedClientId.name: x-expected-client-id
ExpectedClientId.description: Optional equality constraint on the verified client, never a credential. HTTP permits this independently of the actor constraint. Runtime counts at most 255 UTF-16 units and rejects C0/unpaired surrogates; this is the shared trace/identifier rule, not the CLI rule that additionally excludes DEL.

NoStore.description: All JSON responses emitted by this application boundary use this cache policy.

ErrorTrace.description: Present for command-layer errors and equals body.trace_id; early authentication/input errors may omit it. Read the body trace without assuming this header exists.

ErrorEnvelope.description: The existing five-field serialized error envelope. Details are open JSON diagnostic fields, not a directory record. Early errors can echo a trace that would fail a successful read's stricter trace constraint. Code/message/retryable depend on the failing stage; do not treat a retryable flag as an instruction to retry automatically or substitute credentials.

Error.description: Application JSON error, never a partial directory page. The status-specific descriptions list current known codes, not a new exhaustive error enum.
